races.name: Hamilton Park Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up performer with a bleak record on soft ground (0 wins, 0 places from 3 similar-going runs) and a poor recent form string including an 8th last time out; Lexie Clarkson's 7lb claim helps the weight but does little to address the going and positional concerns.
runners_data.comment: Harb tops our figures on the strength of a win three starts back and has form over today's trip and going. The concern is that his last two efforts, a 6th and then an 8th last time out, have been well below that level.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for this race though its best form has come in a prominent rather than lead role, carrying a STYLE_FIT flag; Nigel Tinkler has just 1 winner from 29 runners over 14 days and only 2 similar-going runs in its record — if it gets comfortable in front on the soft ground it is the primary threat to control the race.
runners_data.comment: Azuinthejungle found his best form of the sequence with a 3rd last time out, better than the 7th two starts back. He has raced over today's trip and going before, and that improving trend makes the case for him, with a stable short on form the concern.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Smart recent third on soft ground is the standout piece of evidence in its favour, and R Mike Smith has 2 winners from 21 runners over 14 days; however, this horse's natural hold-up style has been squeezed into a midfield mapping by the volume of pace-shy horses in the field, tempering confidence that it will get the late run it needs.
runners_data.comment: Ski Angel's last two efforts (2nd, then 3rd) are her most encouraging of the sequence, an upturn on the 5th and 6th before that. She has raced over today's trip and going before, but near the bottom of our figures, making her hard to trust fully.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old wearing headgear (p) whose last 5 runs show no wins and only one place, all on good ground; pushed into a midfield slot by redistribution rather than by inclination, and its true closer profile makes it structurally vulnerable in a race where the soft ground will blunt late finishes.
runners_data.comment: Sixcor sits bottom of our figures, a promising 3rd two starts back not built on when down to 7th last time out. He has raced over today's trip and going before, but with 8th, 9th and 5th also in the mix recently, there's plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Realistic Dream
runners_data.note: A lightly weighted 3-year-old with no wins or places from 4 similar-going runs and a sequence of mid-pack finishes; Oliver Carmichael's 5lb claim provides some compensation but the horse's hold-up style and uninspiring recent form offer limited encouragement in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Realistic Dream has been consistent without threatening to win, mixing regular 5ths and 6ths with the odd 9th, most recently a 6th. She has raced over today's trip and going before and is rated above her modest official mark, though six starts without success leave plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's string is flying with 7 winners from 30 runners over 14 days, and this mare's form string of 2-2-2 in her last three comparable races underlines she is consistently competitive; a 37-day break is worth monitoring but she holds prominent position naturally and the soft ground has not stopped her before.
runners_data.comment: Thunderstorm Katie arrives on three straight runner-up finishes, a marked step up on the 9th and 7th before that, and returns over suitable trip and going. The 37-day gap since, and a sequence still without a win, are the queries against one of the leading threats.

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: Most reliable similar-going record in the field (10 runs, 1 win, 3 places) and won last time out, making her the form pick among the prominent types; Adrian Nicholls has 3 winners from just 6 runners over 14 days and Jack Nicholls knows the yard well, adding a positive trainer-jockey angle.
runners_data.comment: Thornaby Pearl was a good second last time out. He scored three starts back and has framed consistently in between. He has raced over today's trip and going before, making him a leading danger, though he sits behind two rivals on our figures.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Won on soft going over 6f in recent form and possesses genuine hold-up ability that was decisive that day; displaced into a midfield mapping here because the rear is overcrowded with natural closers — the visor is noted, and while the form is live, its chance depends on a pace scenario that does not currently look likely to materialise.
runners_data.comment: Doon The Glen won three starts back and rounded off with a 3rd last time out, sandwiching a below-par 8th in between. He has raced over today's trip and going before, but sits only mid-pack on our figures, more thereabouts than a big threat.

races.paceDynamic: Azuinthejungle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner 5f apprentice handicap on Good To Soft ground at Hamilton, and with Thunderstorm Katie and Thornaby Pearl expected to press from a prominent position, the pace should be honest rather than scorching — a single leader rarely generates a truly searingly fast tempo on soft ground over a minimum trip. Azuinthejungle will dictate from the front but faces a field with considerably more natural pace than can be accommodated: Doon The Glen, Ski Angel, and Sixcor are all genuine hold-up types who have been mapped into midfield positions purely because the rear of the field is overcrowded, meaning their actual race-day positions may be closer to mid-division than genuine back-markers. With a controlled but not dawdling pace set by Azuinthejungle and two genuine prominent racers tracking closely, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort into the Hamilton uphill finish on softening ground — pure hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged by the track topology and the moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Azuinthejungle sets a controlled pace and Thunderstorm Katie and Thornaby Pearl track closely throughout.
scenarios.body: The honest but not punishing tempo on Good To Soft ground plays directly into the hands of horses who can sit just off the leader and pounce in the final furlong up Hamilton's stiff finish; prominent racers avoid the traffic risks that will hamper the redistibuted hold-up types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Azuinthejungle is allowed to find a comfortable rhythm unchallenged and the soft ground blunts the finishing kicks of hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner on soft turf over 5f at Hamilton can establish a decisive lead if the pace is moderate and pursuers are slow to respond; with no horse capable of immediately pressuring Azuinthejungle from an early stage, a wire-to-wire result is plausible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and genuine hold-up horses find clear daylight sooner than expected.
scenarios.body: Ski Angel has the best similar-going profile of the redistributed types and Doon The Glen won on soft going in recent form, giving both a chance if they negotiate traffic and arrive with a late surge; however, both carry the STYLE_FIT discount having been pushed out of their natural role in this race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground slows the tempo dramatically and the field concertinas in the final 2f, making the race a lottery.
scenarios.body: A severe easing of ground conditions or an unusually dawdling pace could neutralise positional advantages and allow unconsidered runners from mid-division to get involved; Realistic Dream and Harb, both struggling on similar ground in recent outings, remain unlikely beneficiaries even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Thunderstorm Katie and Thornaby Pearl — both prominent types with strong recent form — must be tracked from the stalls; if either secures a clean position just off Azuinthejungle's shoulder they become the most dangerous horses in the race.

Azuinthejungle is technically rated as racing out of its optimum role and has only 2 similar-going runs in its history — if the soft ground catches it out mid-race, the pace it sets could collapse rapidly and benefit the hold-up types.

Doon The Glen and Ski Angel are natural hold-up horses artificially placed in midfield on the map; watch whether they drift back to their true position at the start, which would leave them with significantly more ground to make up than their nominal mapping suggests.

The soft ground at Hamilton on this straight 5f course historically blunts the speed of front-runners in the final furlong — if Azuinthejungle's stride shortens noticeably at the 1f pole, the prominent chasers rather than late closers are best placed to capitalise given the field's structural composition.

races.name: John & Margaret McCluskey Memorial Celebrations EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.note: Showed decent ability on Good to Soft at York (2nd) and has experience over six furlongs before dropping back to five, so the shorter trip on similar ground here is the key question; lightly raced at two with an unknown running style, Jack Nicholls takes the ride for K.R. Burke whose 14-day strike rate of 7/51 is solid.

runners_data.name: Hell Of A Spin
runners_data.note: A debut second at Carlisle, which is Oisin McSweeney's only datapoint on this horse, tells us she handles a track with character; Adrian Keatley's team have fired this filly into this race just 14 days on, suggesting she's in good order, and her style is unclassified — whoever shows most pace here, she could be involved.

runners_data.name: River Jordan
runners_data.note: Pulled up last of seven on soft ground at Ripon on debut 98 days ago, so the layoff and the single poor run on similar going are both concerns; Connor Beasley is a booking that keeps her in the picture, but she must show significant improvement to feature at the sharp end of this sprint.

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's juveniles often improve with racing and Calef has three runs to his name, all on good ground, placing third on debut and fourth twice since; genuinely a closer by nature, he is shown in midfield here only because the field is stacked with hold-up horses and the back of the race is congested — his ability to deliver a finish depends on the pace being honest enough to tow him into contention.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: Bred for speed — his sire is Havana Grey — and has shown a mix of placing (2nd at Beverley) and disappointing (7th at Carlisle); a true hold-up performer whose preferred tactical role is squeeze through late, but the race shape here is unlikely to provide that clean sprint needed, which tempers confidence even if the nine-day turnaround from John & Sean Quinn's yard suggests freshness.

runners_data.name: My Mate Fitz
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott retains the ride after a fourth on soft ground at Carlisle, which is the most relevant piece of form in this field from a going perspective; instinctively a horse that wants a pace to chase, he has been shown in midfield only because genuine closers fill the back of the map — the risk is that without a strong gallop, he simply arrives too late on Hamilton's undulating five furlongs.

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's juvenile finished sixth on debut at Carlisle over six furlongs on good ground, and now drops to five on softer — the shorter trip on a sharper surface is potentially an improvement angle; Jack Garritty rides and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 6/64 is respectable, but there is very little form here to assess with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field, none of Casino Star, Hell Of A Spin, My Mate Fitz, Havana Gift, Calef, River Jordan or Onslaught has shown the desire or ability to dominate from the front, meaning the early gallop is likely to be modest and the race will compress into a sprint finish off the final bend. On Good To Soft ground over five furlongs at Hamilton — a track where the downhill run encourages a bunched, pacy finish rather than a wire-to-wire display — the absence of a genuine pace-setter means the tempo will be dictated by whoever shows most natural early speed on the day, likely Casino Star or Hell Of A Spin, neither of whom has established that role convincingly. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically fulfil that role: My Mate Fitz, Havana Gift and Calef are all genuine come-from-behind horses mapped to midfield simply because the rear of the field is overcrowded, and their true style may not be deliverable here. The tactical verdict is clear: with a contested but not fast early pace on softish ground and a sprint finish likely, horses with the tactical speed to travel prominently and finish strongly through the race — rather than true closers needing a strong gallop — are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of a front-runner produces a slow-burn first half and the race ignites only in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Without a genuine leader, the field will dawdle before a sharp sprint kicks off approaching the Hamilton straight, suiting runners with natural tactical speed who can accelerate quickly over a short distance on soft ground; Casino Star and Hell Of A Spin, both with form over similar conditions, are best equipped to produce that late kick from a prominent position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Stolen
scenarios.trigger: If one runner, most likely Casino Star or Hell Of A Spin, breaks smartly and establishes a soft lead without serious pressure
scenarios.body: Hamilton's downhill configuration means an uncontested leader on Good To Soft could dictate a comfortable tempo and simply stay out of trouble to the line, as the hold-up horses behind — Calef, My Mate Fitz and Havana Gift — are unlikely to be close enough to close in time; soft ground extends the advantage of a horse that avoids the traffic clustered at the rear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If a quicker-than-expected early gallop develops and the leaders pay for it inside the final furlong
scenarios.body: Should the pace prove genuinely honest for soft ground, the horses mapped to midfield — My Mate Fitz, Havana Gift and Calef — could arrive late, though their redistribution from the rear means they may not achieve enough separation from the pack to produce a clean finish; My Mate Fitz showed soft-ground ability at Carlisle and retains the best profile among this group if the race genuinely sets up for closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so inconsistent that the field arrives at the line in a heap with no horse able to establish clear momentum
scenarios.body: On soft ground with no natural leader, a stop-start gallop can produce a wide-open finish where positional luck and a clean run matter more than any tactical pattern; in this scenario runners who manage to find daylight early, such as Onslaught or River Jordan, could gain from the chaos, though both are limited by exposed moderate form.

watchPoints.text: Casino Star and Hell Of A Spin — if either breaks smartly and establishes an uncontested early lead, the field's lack of a true front-runner means no rival is likely to challenge them for that position, making the lead potentially very soft and lucrative.

My Mate Fitz, Havana Gift and Calef are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield positions on the map — watch for them to become boxed in during a slow-paced, bunched run that removes their ability to execute a clean finishing move.

River Jordan — the 98-day absence combined with a poor solo run on soft ground creates a significant unknown; if she has improved significantly at home her price may be instructive, but blindly following her would be risky.

Going listed as Soft in the race header but the course's own going report states Good to Soft for the 6:15 — confirm the official going board figure at the track before drawing firm conclusions, as even that small distinction can affect hold-up horses' ability to close on Hamilton's straight.

Onslaught drops from six furlongs to five and from good to softer ground — both are unknowns, but the combination of a sharper trip and a field with no genuine pace could suit a horse that simply travels well rather than needing a true test of stamina.

races.name: Rocca Restaurant & Ora Bar Hamilton Handicap

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: The race pivots around this horse — sole front-runner with a solid soft-ground record over 6f, 3 placed runs in 15 similar-going starts, and Jack Garritty booked; carries 140lbs but his style-fit score of 0.93 reflects that this uncontested lead scenario is actually where he operates best, making that tag a positive rather than a concern here.
runners_data.comment: Ingleby Archie won last time out to cap a rock-solid sequence of finishes - second, third and fourth in the starts before that. He has claims over today's trip and going, and although a 21-day gap follows that success, the clear upward trend in his form makes him a major threat.

runners_data.name: Not Me
runners_data.note: Career best form has come over shorter trips on soft (1W at 8f/SOF) but he's a hold-up type who handles the going, and with Jack Nicholls (5) aboard for a trainer who is 0/8 in the last 14 days, momentum is limited; 29 days off is neutral but the step down in trip from recent starts needs proving.
runners_data.comment: Not Me bounced back to win last time out after a run of modest finishes, including two fifths and an unplaced effort further back. He has claims over today's going, and though a 29-day break follows that success, the improvement makes him a leading danger.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a genuine recent winning thread (1-2-1 in last four 6f starts) and Connor Beasley is a shrewd pilot in this type of sprint handicap; by nature a closer who will be tracking from further back than ideal — the soft ground suits based on that 6f/SOF win in the hist, but the gap from off the pace may be too wide to bridge today.
runners_data.comment: Iris Dancer rates bottom of these figures despite having won twice in her last six starts, with a placed second between those victories. She has claims over today's trip and going, though last time out's below-par sixth is a concern heading into this race.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 3yo wore a visor and returned a win last time, but soft going is a question mark given that best form reads on Good — only 8 days since last run suggests freshness, yet the redistribution away from the rear means this confirmed hold-up runner must navigate further forward than Mark Winn would naturally choose.
runners_data.comment: Come On Over won last time out to end a run of modest form that had included finishes as low as eighth and unplaced. He has claims over today's trip and going, and having resurfaced quickly just eight days later, the improvement last time is the headline for this outsider.

runners_data.name: Eartha
runners_data.note: The outstanding concern in the field — 358 days off the track, a solitary visit to soft going produced a 19th-place finish, and Fahey's operation is 4/50 in 14 days showing no hot streak; Oisin McSweeney takes the ride but this mare has to prove she retains ability after nearly a year away before being considered.
runners_data.comment: Eartha's recent starts read modestly on paper - no better than eighth in any of her last four - but our figures rate her clear of this field and well above her current mark. She has claims over today's distance, and despite a near year-long absence, the upside in her figures makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 4yo ran only 5 days ago and sports a solid recent run (1st at 7f/GOO, 3rd at 7f/SOF), giving genuine confidence on cut ground; Rhys Elliott (5) is an apprentice claim but Ashen's natural closing style places it in compromised territory positionally — the 6f trip is a slight shortening from its best winning distance.
runners_data.comment: Ashen won three starts back and has since added a solid placed effort, a fourth his latest run just five days ago. He has experience of today's distance, and with barely a break since his last outing, that fitness edge makes him a real threat to all.

races.paceDynamic: Ingleby Archie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 6f handicap on Good To Soft at Hamilton, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, he is set to stride into an uncontested, controlled gallop from the gates. The remaining five runners are all hold-up or wait-and-pounce types by nature, meaning the pace is likely to be honest but not pressured, with Ingleby Archie dictating tempo entirely on his own terms. On soft-leaning ground over six furlongs at Hamilton, a sustainable lead with no battle for early position typically rewards the horse at the front or tracking closest — the prominent-to-lead profile is the clear beneficiary here. Come On Over, Ashen, and Iris Dancer are genuine hold-up horses forced into a midfield map position because the field contains more deep-closers than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear, so their ability to access their preferred tactical berth is genuinely compromised.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Archie Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie bowls along at a controlled, uncontested gallop and the hold-up horses cannot generate enough momentum off a steady pace on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Ingleby Archie sets his own rhythm with no pressure, the soft ground blunts the closers' finishing kicks, and racing prominently throughout becomes an insurmountable advantage over six furlongs at Hamilton.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively quick despite the lack of a challenger and the closers get an unusually strong tow into the race.
scenarios.body: The ground softening the surface enough to level the field, the hold-up horses find their finishing runs arrive at the right moment and overhaul the front-runner in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Tracker Arrives
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up type secures a closer-than-usual pitch and uses the prominent position to grind out a winning challenge as the leader ties up.
scenarios.body: Soft ground rewards those who travel within themselves and pick up late, and a horse like Ashen — capable on cut — lands in a position that suits better than its natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Blows Race Open
scenarios.trigger: If the field goes unexpectedly hard early, Ingleby Archie is burned off, and the race degenerates into an attritional test that scrambles the outcome.
scenarios.body: With all rivals playing wait-and-see tactics and Ingleby Archie potentially over-pressed by his own exuberance, a long-striding hold-up type with soft-ground stamina could pick up the pieces late.

watchPoints.text: Ingleby Archie's ability to control tempo entirely uncontested is the race-defining factor — watch whether he is allowed to dictate or if Come On Over or Ashen are ridden more aggressively than expected to apply early pressure.

Eartha's 358-day absence makes her a serious unknown quantity; watch market moves at the off — significant support would imply a confident stable but any drift should reduce confidence in her participation meaningfully affecting the result.

Iris Dancer's recent form (1-2-1 in last four) makes her statistically the most in-form runner, but watch where Connor Beasley positions her in the early stages — if she is forced wider or deeper than usual by the crowded hold-up group, her finishing effort may be neutralised.

With five hold-up horses chasing one front-runner, watch for a bunching effect in the back straight — if several of the midfield group are checked or blocked, a clear run to the outside in the final two furlongs becomes a significant positional advantage.

Not Me is stepping back to 6f from recent 8-10f trips — watch the first two furlongs to see if he settles comfortably in his hold-up role or shows signs of ring-rustiness that might compromise his late challenge.

races.name: racingtv.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has consistent form at 10-12f on good ground but has not won in his last five starts; as a hold-up horse he will need the front two to tire on the climb home, and his 144lb burden is also worth factoring against him.|
runners_data.comment: Prince Of The Seas was third last time out and tops our figures for this test, race fit after just eight days off. Winless in his last five starts, but he has form over today's trip and looks the one to beat on pure figures.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jura
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner boasts confirmed front-running habits but has zero wins or places in two runs on soft or similar going, and at 1m5f — a trip that stretches his stamina profile — the STYLE_FIT flag signals a potential mismatch between his natural role and the demands of today.|
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Jura was runner-up last time out, winless in her last five starts, but she has claims back at today's trip and going. Her rating puts her right in this fight, though a 24-day absence is the one blot on her claims.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Acklam
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby's five-year-old has two wins and two placings from five runs on soft or analogous going, giving him the strongest sim-going record in the field; he is a natural hold-up type who will need the pace to be sufficient to close, but the going is firmly in his favour.|
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Acklam ranks second on our figures and has landed one of his last five starts, his form fluctuating but sharp enough to feature. A below-par effort last time can be forgiven, and with claims over today's trip and going after a 28-day break, he's a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old arrives in strong form — a win then a runner-up from his last two starts — and is the only horse in the field combining a prominent running style with recent winning form, which makes his ability to track Spirit Of Jura into a prime position the key tactical advantage in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Dunkeld Dreamer won last time out, one of two victories in her last six starts, and she holds form on today's going. A 28-day break is the only query, otherwise she looks a big threat on pure figures.

runners_data.name: Sure And Stedfast
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer whose natural style has been compressed into a midfield slot by the weight of hold-up types in this field; two placed efforts from four runs on soft or similar ground show ability, but racing against his grain at a modest pace makes his task significantly harder than the map implies.|
runners_data.comment: Sure And Stedfast rates the outsider of these six on our figures, though he has been game in defeat with two seconds and a third among his last five starts. Still winless in that sequence and quick back within a fortnight, he needs more to trouble these rivals.

runners_data.name: Ameilya
runners_data.note: Stuart Coltherd's five-year-old has experience at staying trips and has won on soft ground, but her true hold-up inclinations leave her at the mercy of a race shape that offers little space to come from behind; the STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 reflects that today's tactical requirements cut against how she performs at her best.|
runners_data.comment: Ameilya has failed to threaten in her last four starts, no better than sixth in that sequence and winless throughout. She does have experience of today's going and a quick 11-day turnaround, but there's little in that form to suggest she can trouble these rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Jura is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, uncontested, will dictate a controlled, honest pace over 1m5f on Good to Soft ground at Hamilton. With no rival willing or able to push forward and challenge for the lead, the tempo is likely to be sustainable rather than searching — a steady gallop that keeps the field compressed and offers little opportunity for genuine hold-up horses to exploit a gap in the final stages. Dunkeld Dreamer is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track Spirit Of Jura closely in second, giving the front two a tactical advantage through the race. This shape — a lone, unhurried front-runner setting a moderate pace with a small field — strongly favours prominent racers and horses with a forward cruising speed who can travel into a good position; true hold-up types will find it difficult to generate the momentum needed to close when the gap to the leaders is never allowed to grow. The field contains more hold-up types than can comfortably sit at the rear with a meaningful advantage, with Sure And Stedfast and Ameilya both genuine hold-up horses who are effectively pushed into a midfield role against their natural grain — Spirit Of Jura and Dunkeld Dreamer are most likely to actually secure the positions that matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jura Controls, Dunkeld Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Jura dictates a fair but uncontested gallop and Dunkeld Dreamer tracks in a perfect position throughout.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Jura sets a sustainable tempo, and Dunkeld Dreamer — the only other horse naturally inclined to race prominently — sits a length or two off the pace and has first run turning for home, giving it the decisive positional advantage. This shape suits horses who travel into contention rather than closing from off the pace, and with no pace battle to burn the frontrunners out, the race resolves itself in the final two furlongs for those already in the first two.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Jura sets a genuinely slow early tempo, compressing the field and allowing hold-up horses to stay in touch with minimal effort.
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure, the entire field races in a cluster and the hold-up label becomes irrelevant, meaning Prince Of The Seas or Spirit Of Acklam can find themselves naturally in contention without having to make up ground. A late burst from a horse with strong finishing form on similar going then becomes the decisive factor, and Spirit Of Acklam's two wins from five runs on soft or similar ground give it a clear claims in this version of events.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stacks It
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Jura, asked to race prominently against its natural profile at this longer trip, fades and the race opens up turning for home.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Jura's STYLE_FIT flag and limited form on soft ground over a staying trip raises the genuine possibility it cannot sustain its position, and if it capitulates, it may drag Dunkeld Dreamer into trouble or leave a vacuum that rewards a horse with latent energy. Prince Of The Seas, the widest hold-up runner with reasonable form over 12f on good ground, would be the chief beneficiary if the race suddenly becomes a true test of finishing stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overrun Leaders Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to soften the front two and the hold-up horses produce genuine late closures.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Sure And Stedfast and Ameilya — both true hold-up horses forced into midfield against their natural role — to find their rhythm despite the compromised map position, and the STYLE_FIT and REDISTRIBUTED flags on both materially reduce its likelihood. Even if the tempo is honest, neither horse has the sim-going form or recent profile to suggest they can deliver a winning finish from a position they are unlikely to occupy naturally.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Of Jura's soft-ground record (0 wins, 0 places from 2 runs) combined with the step up to 1m5f makes it a genuine risk that it cannot sustain the lead it is expected to set — watch for signs of it weakening turning for home.

Dunkeld Dreamer's 3-year-old weight allowance at 125lbs versus older rivals is notable — monitor whether it has the physical scope to see out 1m5f on soft ground having only previously won at shorter.

Sure And Stedfast and Ameilya are both listed as true hold-up types but are effectively racing out of role today — if either drifts back to their natural position rather than holding midfield, they may find themselves with too much ground to make up.

With only six runners and a lone confirmed front-runner, the pace could be dangerously slow in the early stages — watch the early sectionals, as a muddling gallop would compress the field and favour whoever has the best turn of foot in the final furlong rather than the most prominent position.

races.name: Get Your Tickets For Cube Glass Ladies Night Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaleido
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4-year-old has a placed effort over 9f on Good going and steps up in trip here, which the form suggests suits; races prominently but has returned figures of 6, 9, 10 in most recent starts so needs to find improvement, though the longer 1m½f trip could unlock more.|
runners_data.comment: Kaleido heads our figures on the back of a runner-up effort last time out, though his four starts before that were modest. He races from stall one over today's distance, quick back inside a fortnight, and is still winless in his last five starts despite that pleasing latest run.

runners_data.name: Zowal
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Soft at Beverley and carries legitimate soft-ground form credentials — the strongest in the field for these conditions; a true hold-up horse who will sit off the pace and needs a searching gallop to come from behind, which may not materialise with Lucky Camino alone in front.|
runners_data.comment: Zowal shows an improving profile among these six. He was third last time out, having scored two starts back. He has claims over today's trip and going, and though a 21-day break is the only query, that upward trend makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Quiet Resolve
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 8-9f on Good and Soft ground with solid form figures, and trainer Alan Brown is a small-yard operator sending this horse 39 days fresh; by nature a prominent racer, but the field's pace composition means Quiet Resolve is likely to be shuffled back further than Alan Brown would wish, racing in unnatural territory.|
runners_data.comment: Quiet Resolve sits second on our figures, and although last time out was below-par, the form before that reads well with a runner-up effort and a win among his last five starts. He has claims over today's trip and going, but a 39-day layoff is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Lucky Camino
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3-year-old has placed in all three career starts including on Soft ground over 8f, and this step up to 1m½f looks tailored; the lone front-runner, operating at a 0.90 style fit but still the horse best positioned to secure the lead — Kevin Stott is an excellent tactical rider who will set a measured, controlling tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Lucky Camino rates only fifth of six on our figures, though he has been far from disgraced with two seconds and a third in his last three starts. Still winless in that sequence, he does have claims over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie sends this 5-year-old in good form after a recent win, but its natural instinct to race prominently cannot be satisfied in a field already featuring Lucky Camino and Kaleido ahead of it; effectively forced into a mid-pack role on a horse that has not demonstrated the ability to win from off the pace, and an OR of 66 is the lowest in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Sanafi Zabeel rates bottom of these six on our figures despite boasting two wins among his last five starts, though a well-beaten ninth last time out is the concern. He does have experience of today's distance and can't be entirely written off in this sort of company.

runners_data.name: Showcasing Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3-year-old is a consistent placer — four seconds in the last five — but the most recent run was a blank and all those placed efforts came on Standard or Slow AW surfaces; soft turf is a genuine unknown, and as a hold-up horse Connor Beasley will need a lot of luck in running in this small field.|
runners_data.comment: Showcasing Star strung together three runner-up efforts in a row but has since faded, finishing seventh and then unplaced in his last two starts. He does have experience of today's distance and a swift 12-day turnaround, though the recent dip in form is the obvious concern.

races.paceDynamic: Lucky Camino is the sole confirmed front-runner here and should dictate from the outset at Hamilton's 1m½f trip, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead. The going is Good to Soft throughout the card despite the official race description showing Soft, meaning the ground will be testing enough to reward a horse who settles into a rhythm rather than burning up energy fighting for position. Kaleido will press from a prominent position, but the shape is effectively Lucky Camino's to control — a sustainable, uncontested gallop that sets up a race where those who can travel close to the pace and pick up cleanly hold a major advantage. This race shape strongly favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can capitalise on a genuine but measured pace — hold-up horses will need everything to go right. Note that Quiet Resolve and Sanafi Zabeel are genuine prominent types who cannot all be accommodated in that position; Lucky Camino and Kaleido are best placed to actually secure prominent berths, with the other two likely to find themselves further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lucky Camino Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lucky Camino leads uncontested, sets a measured pace and the field never seriously challenges for the front.
scenarios.body: Lucky Camino dictates on his own terms into soft ground, conserving energy through the long home straight, and has enough in reserve to repel challengers; his three-run form string of 2-2-3 shows consistent place-getting at this level and the step up to 1m½f looks a natural fit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Kaleido or another prominent runner times the move to perfection and runs Lucky Camino out of it in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The soft ground gradually takes its toll on Lucky Camino's front-running effort and a horse sitting a length or two off the pace finds the extra reserves to collar him; David O'Meara's Kaleido showed a placed effort over 9f on Good and will appreciate this longer trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to burn off the leader and leave the door open for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Zowal won on Soft over 8f and has the profile to pick up late ground, but this scenario requires Lucky Camino to have over-cooked the pace, which looks unlikely given the small field and lack of pace pressure; Showcasing Star has multiple placed efforts but soft-ground form is thin and the form string shows a recent blank.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Quiet Resolve or Sanafi Zabeel push aggressively for a prominent position early, causing a rougher-than-expected gallop.
scenarios.body: Either horse fighting for position would disrupt Lucky Camino's rhythm and create a more contested tempo, but both are racing out of their natural role given the field configuration and the soft ground makes early energy expenditure costly; even if the pace is disrupted, neither redistributed runner is well-placed to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Lucky Camino leads alone with no pace pressure — if Kevin Stott is allowed to set a completely unchallenged tempo, he could control the race from wire to wire and any horse that fails to travel close to him is at serious risk of being out of contention.|

Quiet Resolve and Sanafi Zabeel may both push forward early to try to claim prominent positions, creating a brief flashpoint in the opening furlong; watch whether either manages to slot in on Lucky Camino's quarters or is forced to drop off the pace entirely.|

Zowal's soft-ground win is the most relevant form in the field for today's conditions, but as a genuine hold-up horse in a small six-runner field, Dougie Costello will need a gap to appear in the straight — with Lucky Camino potentially clear, there may simply be no strong pace to chase down.|

Showcasing Star's repeated placed efforts on AW surfaces look less transferable to Good to Soft turf at Hamilton — monitor market moves to see if the market reflects any trainer confidence or absence thereof for the ground change.|

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who sets the entire agenda here; Iain Jardine has had 8 winners from 29 runners in the last 14 days and the horse's sole similar-going win came at this sort of trip, though a style-fit score of 0.93 reflects she is asked to do a job she does not always relish — nonetheless she has every tactical advantage with no rival for the lead.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out, with a fourth two starts back before it, gives this mare a workable profile. The yard is in good touch at 28% over the past fortnight, and Second Fiddle is effective back over this trip and ground, drawn 4, though yet to win in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good ground last time out so the step up in trip is logical; Kevin Stott is a shrewd rider who will hunt an economical position, but zero wins or places from 15 starts on soft-comparable ground is a stark stamina-in-testing-conditions flag at this mile-and-a-half distance.
runners_data.comment: Daring Leader won last time out, a breakthrough after a string of modest form beforehand. He has raced over today's trip before, but sits near the bottom of these figures, making it hard to trust him fully.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's nine-year-old has finished fifth or worse in all six recent runs including three consecutive fifths on Good ground; the horse's true racing style is hold-up but with three other closers in the field it is squeezed toward midfield on the map, meaning it faces an awkward compromise between instinct and positioning.
runners_data.comment: Hostelry has been the picture of consistency - three straight 5ths and a 4th before that - and returns over suitable trip and ground. Rated above her modest official mark, though a stable out of form and six starts without a win temper the case.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent runner from the Quinn yard wearing headgear, returning after 33 days off; it has shown placed form on soft ground and on Tapeta and will likely slot in directly behind Second Fiddle, making it the most naturally positioned horse to pounce if the leader weakens late.
runners_data.comment: Positive Thoughts heads our figures, having been runner-up five starts back and rallying to 5th last time out after a below-par 9th in between. She has raced over today's trip before and, a 33-day break aside, remains the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's four-year-old has been beaten into ninth on two of its last three starts on soft ground and its form figures of 586-89 make grim reading; a genuine hold-up runner by nature but crowded out at the rear of the field's map, it carries the lowest OR in the race and faces an uphill task from every angle.
runners_data.comment: Defence Missile is rated above his modest official mark, the case for him as a leading danger, and he has raced over today's trip and going before. The concern is a run of finishing positions that has drifted the wrong way, down to 9th last time out.

runners_data.name: Amber Hamur
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell has had four winners from 29 runners in the past fortnight and Connor Beasley is an experienced northern handler; returned just eight days ago with a second over 8f on Good, so the extra half-furlong and softer ground are both unexplored territory for this three-year-old, which adds meaningful uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Amber Hamur ended a run of modest efforts with a good second last time out, having managed only 5th, 5th, 4th and 6th before that. She has raced over today's trip before, but sits only mid-table on our figures, leaving a little more to prove.

runners_data.name: Ten Sixty Six
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has a busy recent record with form figures of 9-9794 and has struggled to make an impact across multiple trips and ground types; it is a natural hold-up horse by inclination but finds itself mapped to midfield given the congestion at the rear, and Mark Winn will need significant improvement on a career best RPR of 71 to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Ten Sixty Six sits bottom of our figures, though she found her best effort last time out with a 4th after four runs no better than 7th. She has raced over today's trip before, but remains without a win and has most to find.

races.paceDynamic: Second Fiddle is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is almost certain to stride into a clear lead from the outset and dictate a steady, controlled tempo on the Good To Soft Hamilton turf. Positive Thoughts is prominent by style and may attempt to track her, but the rest of the field is overwhelmingly held-up in nature, meaning Second Fiddle faces no serious early challenge for the rail. This field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate at the rear — Ten Sixty Six, Hostelry, and Defence Missile are all true come-from-behind horses who are likely to be forced closer to the pace than they would ideally want, compromising their finishing kicks. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone, uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable gallop on soft ground over a mile and a half strongly favours horses who can race prominently and conserve energy, rather than those relying on a late, powerful surge from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Second Fiddle Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Second Fiddle dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent trackers cannot sustain a challenge from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Second Fiddle settles beautifully in front having faced zero early pressure, and the soft ground saps stamina from the hold-up types who have been forced to race against their natural style; the pace is exactly right for a front-runner who relaxes and quickens when asked.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts or a close-tracking runner stalks Second Fiddle throughout and outstays her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse that sits a length or two off the uncontested leader conserves energy in the soft conditions and arrives fresh at the two-pole, whereas Second Fiddle has been alone in front and begins to tie up; the one-and-a-half-mile trip on soft ground tips the balance toward a resolute stayer who travels held up just behind the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Second Fiddle's uncontested lead paradoxically means a slow early tempo and a sprint finish that rewards a horse accelerating from the back.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race can compress the field into a tight bunch turning in, and any hold-up runner who manages to secure a clear run and produce a sharper turn of foot in the final two furlongs could pick off a tiring leader; Amber Hamur and Daring Leader are the most realistic candidates, though the soft ground and their tendency to be further back than ideal make this scenario genuinely low probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Second Fiddle goes too fast early due to a lack of pace-reading and the whole field closes rapidly in the straight.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically hot early tempo on soft ground burns Second Fiddle off in the final quarter-mile, and the race becomes a messy finish among horses who have been shuffled out of position throughout; Defence Missile or Ten Sixty Six could theoretically benefit, but their redistribution from natural hold-up positions means they are unlikely to be ideally placed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Second Fiddle's early pace-setting is the fulcrum of the entire race — if she bowls along uncontested at a genuine gallop on soft ground she could prove very hard to peg back, but if she is allowed to idle in front a late charge becomes more viable.

Positive Thoughts has headgear on and returns after 33 days; if Dougie Costello presses Second Fiddle early rather than tracking quietly, it could inject more pace than the map anticipates and significantly alter the race shape.

Three genuine hold-up horses — Ten Sixty Six, Hostelry, and Defence Missile — are all competing for the same ground at the rear; any interference or traffic in the straight could eliminate all three simultaneously.

The going is confirmed Good To Soft across the card at Hamilton tonight, which should not inconvenience the front-runner unduly but will test the stamina of horses who have to make up ground in the final two furlongs.

Daring Leader's single win came over 8f on Good ground; with tonight's trip a full half-mile longer on softer footing, watch for Kevin Stott positioning unusually close to the pace to compensate for any stamina doubt over the extra distance.

races.name: Follow Us On X At HamiltonParkRC Handicap

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up performer with legitimate soft-ground form (5/15 in similar conditions), the veteran carries top-weight at 142lbs and Jim Goldie has had six winners from 36 runners in the past 14 days, suggesting the yard is in form; suited to a sprint-finish scenario but needs the field to come back to him.|
runners_data.comment: Spanish Hustle heads our figures for this event despite modest recent form, with a fourth his best effort in his last five starts. He does have claims over today's trip and going, and races within three weeks of his latest outing, though little in that form inspires real confidence.

runners_data.name: Jujubella
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partners this five-year-old filly who finished runner-up on her only soft-ground outing, though her true racing style is a deep hold-up and she has been pushed into a midfield mapping here due to overcrowding at the rear — that positional compromise, reflected in a 0.93 style-fit, means she is less likely to secure the ground she truly needs in a slowly-run affair.|
runners_data.comment: Jujubella's form has been on an upward curve, climbing from two below-par efforts into a fifth, a third, and a narrow second last time out. She has claims over today's trip and going, and though still winless in that sequence, the progressive shape of her runs makes her our selection.

runners_data.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners_data.note: A lightly-weighted three-year-old (129lbs) with a win and two places in nine soft-ground runs from four attempts, Iain Jardine's gelding wears blinkers and has been stepping up in trip progressively — Jack Nicholls (5) taking the mount gives a 5lb claimer's weight advantage, and the horse's best form has come when able to sit just off the pace and pick up.|
runners_data.comment: Ibn Altheeb was third last time out and has a win in this sequence of five starts, giving him claims on figures alone. He does have form over today's trip and going, but a 32-day absence and modest placings in between are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Mr Moonshine
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's three-year-old has run consistently enough at 8-9f but has never won, and while his soft-going record includes a placed effort, his natural style is a hold-up which the race shape here is unlikely to accommodate cleanly given the redistribution flag and a 0.90 style-fit score.|
runners_data.comment: Mr Moonshine has been a picture of consistency, finishing no better than second but no worse than fifth across his last five starts, still winless in that sequence. He has claims over today's going, though a 32-day absence is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Clocker
runners_data.note: An unknown quantity tactically — Cian Horgan (5) takes the ride for Edward Bethell, who has had two from 30 in the past fortnight — and with four runs all producing mid-pack finishes there is little guide to whether he will go forward; if he does show early pace he becomes the key pace-setter in this otherwise leaderfree contest, making him a shape-defining runner.|
runners_data.comment: Clocker rates bottom of this field on our figures, without a win and no better than fourth in any of her last four starts. She does have experience of today's going, but a modest profile and a 32-day break make her hard to fancy against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley rides this Charlie Johnston three-year-old who actually has a soft-ground win on his record (9f, soft) and ran second in a 12f start, suggesting he handles the trip and conditions well; like the other hold-up types he has been placed into the midfield mapping rather than the rear, and with a 0.91 style-fit flag the risk is that he cannot settle in his preferred ground in a slowly-run race, though his proven winning ability on this going makes him one of the more attractive profiles in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Port Darwin rates towards the bottom on our figures but did land a win two starts back, in a mixed sequence of results either side. He has claims over today's trip and going, though the patchy profile makes him hard to fully trust here.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner across all six runners and three genuine hold-up types — Jujubella, Mr Moonshine, and Port Darwin — redistributed to midfield because the rear of the field is oversubscribed, this 1m3f Hamilton contest on soft ground is set to be run at a hesitant, muddling gallop from the outset. Spanish Hustle, Ibn Altheeb, and Clocker (style unknown) offer no natural pace-setter, meaning the field will likely crawl early before a sprint develops in the straight, compressing the race into a short stamina test rather than a true test of staying ability. Clocker's unknown style is the wildcard — if he shows any forward inclination he could inject the only meaningful tempo, but even then six runners on soft ground with no genuine front-runner points toward a slowly-run, bunched affair. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel mid-to-handy and produce a sharp late burst, rewarding those comfortable making their move from off a compressed pace rather than pure hold-up types who need a genuine searching gallop to peel off the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Messy Sprint-Finish Bunched
scenarios.trigger: If the field dawdles early and the race resolves into a sprint from the two-furlong pole with no horse getting a clear rail advantage.
scenarios.body: The compressed tempo on soft ground means positions entering the straight are everything, and horses who can quicken sharply from a handy spot will have a decisive edge over those stuck wide or too deep in a six-runner field; Port Darwin's recent soft-ground win at 9f and course-relevant form makes him dangerous if he secures the ideal position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types drops out of contact early but an unexpected injection of pace mid-race creates enough of a genuine gallop to bring a late finisher into play.
scenarios.body: A truer gallop on soft ground would stretch the field and allow a horse tracking from the rear to pick up beaten rivals in the straight; Jujubella's sole placed effort in similar conditions and Kevin Stott's patient riding style are the clevers here, but the low STYLE_FIT rating and redistribution flag temper confidence materially.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Clocker Leads And Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker, with unknown tactical style, shows enough early pace to go forward and dictate a modest but uncontested gallop in a field of six.
scenarios.body: Racing in front against hold-up rivals who cannot naturally get forward would leave Clocker ideally placed turning in, and Edward Bethell's runner has the OR and recent soft experience to hold on if the fractions suit; Ibn Altheeb, carrying a light weight as a three-year-old, could be best of the rest if Clocker sets a tempo that brings late challengers up short.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If unexpected rain overnight or a noticeably deteriorating strip pushes the going officially to Soft and a bold-going type drags the field into a genuine test of 1m3f stamina.
scenarios.body: Under a true stamina test Mr Moonshine's five-race habit of finishing in the front half and his soft-ground course history would come into sharper focus, but his 0W record in similar conditions and STYLE_FIT concern keep this scenario firmly at the margins.

watchPoints.text: Port Darwin and Jujubella are flagged as redistributed hold-up types mapped to midfield — watch whether Connor Beasley and Kevin Stott allow them to drop away early or attempt to ride closer than their natural style, as this will materially alter the race shape for the field behind them.

Clocker's unknown tactical style (style=U) is the race's biggest wildcard — if Cian Horgan elects to take the initiative early and go to the front, the entire complexion of the contest changes from a sprint-finish lottery to a more conventional test.

The soft ground has been confirmed across all Hamilton races today, and six consecutive results on Good To Soft suggest the strip has not deteriorated significantly — but any late rain could push the going to genuinely testing Soft, which would disadvantage Mr Moonshine and Ibn Altheeb over this extended 1m3f trip.

With six runners and no genuine pace, Spanish Hustle's rider Rhys Elliott (5) faces a tactical dilemma — too far back in such a small field and the horse will have insufficient time to close, yet Spanish Hustle's natural style is hold-up; watch the draw and early positioning closely at the start.
